prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1324; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the policyholder reported a collision at an intersection while turning left, with the claimant's vehicle reportedly struck on its driver side. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer and reported neck and back strain.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy record and confirmed the driver involved is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the reported loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who described the same sequence of events as in the first report, with the other vehicle turning across their path. Responding officer's report and statements from the scene confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 4: Photos submitted with the claim show damage that matches the described impact. Some details are visible in the images, though no independent witnesses have come forward to describe the collision.

Entry 5: Requested prior claim and vehicle history. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and no prior injury to the neck or back has been identified in the records received so far.

Entry 6: Medical records show treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of strain. It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash, and the treating provider's causation opinion is still pending.

Entry 7: File remains open pending receipt of the complete medical records and the causation opinion. Next step is to schedule a follow-up call with the claimant to confirm treatment details and any further documentation.
